title: Shurpanakha
hook: the demoness's proposal; Lakshmana's cut; the spiral begins

segments.voice: Yesterday: vanaprastha, the forest stage, and a hut where less was enough. The peace at Panchavati is about to end, and it ends with a visitor.

A woman walks out of the trees at Panchavati. She's a rakshasi, one of the demon people of the forest, and the sister of Ravana, king of Lanka. Her name is Shurpanakha. She sees Rama and falls for him on the spot, and she doesn't hide it. She walks right up and says: marry me. Leave that woman. I'll be your wife, and we'll roam the forest together. It's bold, and sudden. And the next few minutes set off the war that fills the rest of the Ramayana.
screen: `A VISITOR FROM THE TREES.` → `RAVANA'S SISTER.` → `MARRY ME.`

segments.voice: Rama answers with a joke. I'm married, he says, but my brother isn't. Try him. Lakshmana jokes back: why be the wife of a servant? Go back to my brother. She's sent back and forth until she realizes they're laughing at her. Humiliated and furious, she turns on the one she thinks is in the way, Sita, and rushes at her to kill her. Rama stops her and tells Lakshmana to teach her a lesson. Lakshmana cuts off her nose and ears. She runs screaming from the forest, bleeding, to her brother Khara. This is a hard scene, and readers have disagreed about it. Some see Rama and Lakshmana defending Sita from an attack. Others, modern writers among them, are uneasy: the teasing, the cruelty of the punishment, a woman mocked and then maimed. Retellings in different languages handle it differently. Unease here isn't disrespect; it's part of a conversation inside the tradition. Her name means something like the one with nails like winnowing fans, fierce and sharp. Whatever you decide about who was right, look at the chain. A proposal. A joke. A humiliation. An attack. A wound. Next, her brother's army. Then her other brother, Ravana. Then an abduction. Then a war. Each cruelty is a little bigger than the last, and each feels justified to the one doing it. It starts small, often with a laugh. Cruelty compounds.
screen: `A JOKE, SENT BACK AND FORTH.` · `SHE ATTACKS. HE CUTS.` · `READERS STILL DISAGREE.` · `JOKE, WOUND, ARMY, WAR.` · then, large: `CRUELTY COMPOUNDS.`

segments.voice: Think of a small unkind thing, a joke at someone's expense, a cold reply, that grew into something bigger than anyone meant; maybe you did it, maybe it was done to you. Trace the chain, link by link, and ask where it could have stopped: which link could have been a kindness instead?
Shurpanakha. Ravana's sister, whose proposal, mocking and maiming at Panchavati set the whole war in motion.
Your line: cruelty compounds. The chain that began with a laugh isn't finished yet. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus discuss the Shurpanakha episode in many ways: some retellings emphasize the defense of Sita, others, in several Indian languages and in modern writing, tell it with more sympathy for Shurpanakha.
